chapter: Clarinet fingering and the Tio family
title: The Tio family: Papa Tio, Lorenzo and their origins
summary: Papa Tio was the greatest clarinetist of his day and young Lorenzo came up under him; Laurent speculates the family was French or Mexican, and notes the Tranchina's job.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: I was wondering about Lorenzo's father, the old man Tio, and the Papa Tio. Papa Tio was his uncle. Uncle.
Did you get to hear them when you were a boy? Oh, yeah.
Yeah, I did. Yeah, they used to play all up in town there, all around the red light. Just, you know, they'd fade all up in there.
Which was the best one of the family? Who was the best clarinetist, do you think, of all the Tio's?

Oh, well, Papa Tio was supposed to be the greatest round yard at that time. But Lorenzo Tio came up afterwards, under him. The young Lorenzo? Yeah, he was young. He was just, oh, a couple years older than me.

But Papa Tio was way older than me. Yeah. And he came up under Papa Tio, but when he got there he was great. He was one of the best clarinetists you had around you, any style. He played the old boy, the flute and everything.
Did you ever hear any of the Tio's say where they came from, if they might have been Mexican, or if they French or Spanish, or where they might have come from?

Well, the Tio's, well, I'm going to tell you. I'm most part of it, they sort of, could be Mexican or something like that, the type he was, you understand. They could be Mexican or they could be French.
Yeah. You never heard anyone say if they came from Mexico, if they were educated?
But they have some of his people still living here, his sister's still here.
He's got a sister still here in the Seven Ward.
We must try to find her and we could talk to her.

Yeah, we could find her and talk to her, but I'm most positive, he was either French or Mexican type. They were very good. A big family. A really large, pretty large family. And, he always played with Bocard, Peter Bocard over the river by Fess. Well, him and Bocard, they played out at Tranchinas there for 30-some years. I believe it was around about 35 years they stayed out there at Tranchinas on the lake front.
